facts.value: SEK 4,000–7,500/month for student housing (University of Gothenburg); Chalmers estimates SEK 4,000–8,000/month.
SEK 6,000–10,000/month for a small apartment (University of Gothenburg estimate).
SEK 10,525–17,525/month (University of Gothenburg); SEK 14,360–18,360/month incl. course books (Chalmers).
Västtrafik Zone A 30-day youth/student ticket SEK 670 (25% off adult); SEK 335 in the half-price offer until 2 Dec 2026. GU budget lists SEK 645.
Mean temperature about 0.8 °C in January and 18.3 °C in July; about 912 mm precipitation/year, wettest of the four cities (SMHI 1991–2020).
facts.notes: Wikipedia climate table citing SMHI 1991–2020 normals; SMHI's own tables were not reached.

facts.value: University of Gothenburg calls the whole city its campus: central, close to culture, the sea, cafés in Haga and Slottsskogen park.
Swedish not needed for daily life (English widely spoken); learning some Swedish helps socially and for jobs.
A part-time job should not be assumed; budget to support yourself. Non-EU study-permit holders limited to 15 h/week in semesters (rule from June 2026).
No city data. National example: hotel/restaurant agreement floor SEK 153.64–164.30/hour (from 1 Apr 2026, no experience; youth rates under 20). No statutory minimum wage.
facts.source_name: HRF (Hotel and Restaurant Workers' Union) – Gröna Riksavtalet
facts.notes: A collective-agreement wage floor for one sector, not a measured typical student wage; no citable source for typical student pay found.
